tells.tell: Text filled with a gradient (background-clip: text).
A purple-to-blue gradient behind a hero or header.
Emoji used as icons or section markers.
A row of three cards with the same shape, icon slot and text length.
Pure #000 or #fff neutrals where the contract has tinted neutrals.
More than one accent hue competing on one screen.
Every block centered, with no alignment edge.
The same radius and shadow on every block, so nothing stands out.
A small rounded-square icon tile above every heading or card title.
Cards inside cards, so depth stands in for grouping.
A tiny uppercase letter-spaced label above headings, repeated on every section or card.
01 / 02 / 03 numbers next to section headings when the order carries no meaning.
A big number with a small label and an accent, used as decoration rather than the number the user came for.
A thick colored border on one side of a card, list item or callout.
A hairline border plus a wide soft shadow on every card.
A colored glow or radial spotlight behind content or around elements.
A warm cream or beige page background chosen by default, not by the contract.
A grid, dot or stripe pattern background with no map, canvas or measurement under it.
Inter, Roboto, Geist or Space Grotesk used for everything where the contract names no font.
Bounce or elastic easing, or the same fade-up entrance on every section.
Pulsing dots or typing cursors that are not tied to a live process.
Normal states (off, idle, stopped by the user) shown in error red, or meaning carried by color alone.
Copy like streamline, empower, supercharge, seamless, or "X. No Y." punchlines.
No empty, loading, error or long-text handling: blank areas, empty axes, text cut off.
Buttons filled with a gradient or given a colored glow.
Large, dark, blurry shadows that make flat UI float.
Frosted-glass panels (backdrop blur) used as decoration.
Every element rounded to a pill or large radius, so nothing has an edge.
Every button styled as primary in its own color; a destructive action as loud as the safe one.
Charts left in the chart library's default colors and styling.
Each row of a simple list or settings page wrapped in its own card.
Long helper text explaining the obvious, or a row of colored stats crammed into a small block.
Gaps that change from row to row with no scale behind them.
Elements that bob, float or drift with no reason.
Glowing colored borders on a dark background.
